name: Bad Boy
remarks: Top 'Pepper' = white pepper. One German retailer (easycosmetic.de) lists vetiver in the heart instead of cedar; majority of sources give cedar + clary sage. Some sources list amberwood in base, others only tonka + cacao.

name: 212 Men
remarks: Osmoz gives a shorter pyramid (top Lavender, Bergamot, Green Notes; heart Gardenia, Pepper, Ginger; base Sandalwood, Vetiver, Oliban, White Musks); retailers add Grapefruit, Petitgrain, Spices, Violet, Sage, Guaiac Wood, Labdanum. Retailers also credit Ann Gottlieb (fragrance developer/evaluator, not a perfumer) so she was left out of the perfumer field. Perfumer credit not on Osmoz; comes from retailer pages only.

name: Le Beau
remarks: The house publishes only one note per tier (bergamot / coconut wood / tonka bean), so fewer than 2 notes per tier is intentional. Heart is described as 'coconut wood' by the brand; mapped to vocab 'Coconut'. Some retailers label the family Oriental; brand wording is aromatic woody.

name: Le Male Elixir
remarks: Sold as 'Parfum' by the brand, though some retailers (proshop, Sephora DE URL) label it Eau de Parfum. One retailer (ozhairandbeauty) gives a different tier placement (mint top; lavender + benzoin heart; tonka + vanilla base).

name: Invictus Victory Elixir
remarks: Brand now spelled 'Rabanne' (formerly Paco Rabanne); adjust to the site's existing brand label if needed. Marketed as 'Parfum Intense'; some retailers (Sephora ME) call it Eau de Parfum. One retailer dates it 2022, most give 2023. Perfumer not found in any clean source, left null. Top cardamom = green cardamom, pepper = black pepper. Family per retailers 'amber woody spicy'.

name: The Most Wanted Intense
remarks: House publishes a 3-note pyramid (red cardamom / toffee accord / amberwood), so one note per tier. Perfumer could not be confirmed from a clean source (left null). Family not stated by a clean source; 'Amber Woody' chosen from the published notes, treat as editorial. A Perfumania listing describes a different composition (likely mislabeled).

name: L.12.12 Blanc
remarks: Pyramid from Osmoz (which also puts Atlas cedar in the heart; kept only in base to avoid duplication). Retailer summary (grapefruit + cardamom / tuberose + ylang-ylang / vetiver + suede) is consistent. Perfumer not named by any clean source, left null. Incense = oliban.

name: Eros Flame
remarks: New note name introduced: 'Chinotto' (no vocab match). 'Pepper' = black pepper. Lyko puts rosemary in the top; Notino and the Versace-sourced press list put it in the heart. Family label chosen from 'woody spicy' description; some sources say woody oriental.

name: Acqua di Giò Parfum
remarks: Not to be confused with Acqua di Giò Profumo (2014). Ginger extract appears only on The Perfume Shop listing. Incense = olibanum. Brand page not reached directly; notes consistent across retailers.

name: Luna Rossa Ocean
remarks: Notino gives a simplified pyramid (bergamot / iris / vetiver) and calls it a leather fougère. First Prada fragrance under the L'Oréal license.

name: Gentleman Réserve Privée
remarks: Brand pyramid (via Harrods): Italian bergamot essence, Scotch whisky absolute / chestnut, orris concrete, Siam benzoin / Virginia cedar, Haitian vetiver, Indonesian patchouli. Decantx gives a looser base (whiskey, amber, woods). Full official name 'Gentleman Eau de Parfum Réserve Privée'. Family 'Woody Floral' chosen from iris + woods profile (not stated by a clean source).

name: Hero
remarks: House communicates juniper + black pepper (+ bergamot) over a trio of cedarwood oils (Virginia, Atlas, Himalaya), not a classic 3-tier pyramid. Tiers follow the retailer pyramid (bergamot / juniper, black pepper / three cedars). Sephora FR presents juniper and pepper as top notes; Notino FR lists a different, longer pyramid (bergamot, lemon, cardamom / lavender, pepper, juniper, nutmeg / cedar). Year and perfumer confirmed by trade press (Moodie Davitt, Cosmetics Business); launched in travel retail 1 Aug 2021.

name: Kenzo pour Homme
remarks: Currently sold as 'Kenzo Homme' Eau de Toilette (reissued in 2022 with new bottle). Core pyramid from Osmoz (1991 entry: clary sage, rosewood, bergamot, lemon / ozone, thyme, cloves, nutmeg / cedar, balsam fir, sandalwood, white musks). Sephora FR (pine, sandalwood) and Notino FR (marine notes + nutmeg / pine + cedar / sandalwood + labdanum) describe the current version; Sea Notes, Pine and Labdanum added from those. Several reformulations since 1991. Perfumer spelled 'Christian Matthieu' in some sources.

name: Déclaration
remarks: Osmoz classifies it as Woody - Floral Musk; 'Woody Spicy' chosen because cardamom is the documented signature (tendance-parfums). Switch to 'Woody Floral Musk' if strict source adherence is preferred. Caraway is also listed in the top by retailers (omitted to stay within 6 notes). Cumin mentioned by one blog review only; not included. Tea also listed in base by some retailers.

name: Viking
remarks: Creed brand copy: Calabrian bergamot, Sicilian lemon with pink peppercorn, Bulgarian rose and peppermint; woody base of Indian sandalwood and Haitian vetiver. Patchouli from ZGO note list. Notino UK and Scentgrail give a different base (Haitian vetiver, cedarwood, tonka bean, white musk). Pink pepper sits between top and heart depending on source. Some sources credit Olivier and Erwin Creed; kept Olivier Creed per retailer. Family not stated by a clean source.
